# Pandamonium v1.0.75

This patch train splits the Entertainment player from its settings: a dedicated sidebar entry opens the player, and Settings → Entertainment now holds real, per-user defaults instead of acting as a launcher. No backend, route, plugin-contract, dependency, schema, authentication, or stored-data change. Rollback remains signed v1.0.74 and the updater's retained pre-update snapshot.

## MAD-972 — Entertainment: sidebar launcher and Settings defaults

### Problem

The only way into the native Entertainment player was the Settings → Entertainment tab, which closed Settings and opened the fullscreen player. There was no way to set a default provider, anime language, or playback quality, and the player could not be reached from the main sidebar.

### Implementation

A new Entertainment section sits directly above Plugins in the sidebar and opens the player. The Settings → Entertainment tab is now a real panel with default provider, anime language (Sub/Dub), and playback quality controls persisted through the existing per-user `/api/prefs/entertainment` store; the saved defaults are applied when the player opens, and a saved provider auto-opens. The sidebar section and the Settings tab stay hidden until an AniCLI or PandaFlix provider plugin is installed. `static/js/settings.js` no longer launches the player from the tab.

### Product value and UI visibility

The player is one click from the sidebar instead of being buried in Settings, and operators can make it open the way they watch. The sidebar section reuses the existing Plugins section styling and the panel reuses the existing `admin-card` / `settings-row` / `settings-select` language with inline monochrome SVG, so the surface matches the rest of the app.

### Verification

A failure-first source test covered the new sidebar launcher and defaults panel, and two Chromium specs verify that Settings shows the panel (not the player), the sidebar opens the player, one provider opens directly, the two-provider landing works, and saved defaults apply. Focused `tests/test_entertainment.py` passed 11 checks, the full Python suite passed 6,527 tests with five skips, and the full Chromium suite passed 190 tests. Protected PR CI passed Python, browser, syntax, dependency, secret, workflow, container, and image gates.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, schema, environment variable, authentication, proxy contract, or stored-data change was introduced. Defaults are additive per-user preferences under the existing `/api/prefs` store and fall back to Sub/Best quality when unset. Providers remain governed by the installed AniCLI and PandaFlix packages.
